title: Immutable workspace snapshots for Terraform CI with OPA/Conftest feedback loop
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current Terraform CI pipeline runs plan/apply against mutable workspaces and writes state directly to customer S3 buckets. When a policy regression or bad module upgrade slips through, rollbacks are manual, error-prone, and often require customer support intervention. We need an automated, auditable mechanism to snapshot workspace state at plan time, attach OPA/Conftest policy scoring to PRs, and allow safe rollback/restore while preserving audit trails and encrypted state storage.

Goal: Implement immutable workspace snapshot artifacts and a policy feedback loop in the Terraform CI pipeline so that: 1) every plan has a snapshot & immutable metadata for potential rollback, 2) Conftest/OPA can block applies above a configurable failure threshold, 3) operators can trigger automated safe rollbacks when needed, and 4) dashboards surface policy failure trends and rollback events.
acceptance_criteria: CI captures a workspace snapshot object for every PR plan that includes the plan JSON, module versions, provider versions, and a state export where safe to do so (obfuscated as needed)
Conftest/OPA runs as a blocking check with a configurable score threshold; failing PRs post a detailed annotated comment with failing rules and remediation hints
Apply jobs refuse to run unless the associated plan snapshot exists and policy score >= configured threshold
A documented rollback playbook and automated rollback job exist that can restore a snapshot to a read-only separate workspace for verification before promotion
All snapshot artifacts are stored encrypted in S3 with retention and access logs, and a Datadog dashboard surfaces plan success rate, policy_failure_rate, average plan time, and rollback_count
implementation_steps: Design snapshot schema (plan.json, module-lock, provider lock, trimmed state export) and approval for PII/redaction - link to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Workspace+Snapshots
Add snapshot step to GitHub Actions / Atlantis plan runner that uploads artifact to s3://redwood-iac-snapshots/<workspace>/<run-id>/
Integrate OPA/Conftest execution post-plan with unified policy bundle (store in infra repo under /policies) and return structured score and findings
Implement GitHub check integration that annotates PRs with policy results and fails the check when score < threshold set in repo CONFIG or org policy
Modify apply job to require the snapshot reference and a passing policy_score label scanned from PR checks; block applies otherwise
Create an automated rollback workflow that can restore snapshot to a verification workspace and optionally perform an apply in a canary mode after operator approval
Build Datadog dashboard and create alerts: policy_failure_rate > 5% 24h, rollback_count spike, plan_duration > 95th percentile
Add end-to-end tests in the infra CI pipeline that simulate a policy regression and validate snapshot+rollback path
Document runbooks and update onboarding docs for platform and solutions engineers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Storing state exports may expose customer data. Mitigation: Only export state for internal infra (not customer secrets) and run automatic redaction; require KMS encryption and access controls
Risk: Snapshot size may be large causing storage/cost blowup. Mitigation: Trim state export to resource references, compress artifacts, and enforce retention policy (30/90/365 days configurable)
Risk: Policy false positives block legitimate deploys. Mitigation: Provide an emergency bypass with audit logging plus escalation flow and a short-lived allowlist token tied to an SRE oncall
Risk: Operator confusion over rollback semantics. Mitigation: Provide verification workspace and a dry-run restore plus clear playbook steps and Slack runbook automation
notes: Design decision: prefer immutable snapshot artifacts over mutating live state for safer audit and point-in-time recovery
We chose Conftest/OPA for policy checks due to existing org familiarity; consider moving heavy rules to a Rego library hosted in infra/policies
We will initially gate on policy_score >= 0.85 and tune for each repo; enforcement will be gradual (soft-fail with annotations for 2 weeks then block)
Initial implementation will live in a feature branch in https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4128)
testing_plan: Unit tests for snapshot serializer and redaction tool
Integration test that runs plan -> snapshot -> conftest -> apply (in dry-run) in a sandbox AWS account
Chaos test: simulate snapshot upload failure and validate pipeline fail-open vs fail-closed behavior as configured
Manual verification of restore: create verification workspace and run apply with operator approval in staging
rollout_strategy: Phase 1: Opt-in repositories under infra/teams with feature flag; soft enforcement (annotate only) for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Enforce blocking checks for infra/* repos and dedicated VPC deployment repos; monitor false-positive rate
Phase 3: Expand to customer-facing private deployment repos and add automated rollback triggers tied to runtime regression alerts
Provide a rollback toggle in Console: admin users can list snapshots and trigger restores (implementation TBD in a follow-up ticket)
metrics_and_observability: plan_success_rate: percentage of plans that complete without errors
policy_failure_rate: percent of plans failing policy checks
rollback_count: number of automated/manual restores per week
time_to_restore: median time from trigger to verification workspace ready
